original.description: Today, mission ground segment systems face increasingly sophisticated and fast-movingcyber threats that can evade static or rule-based detection tools and overwhelm traditionalrecovery procedures. As attacks grow more pervasive, dynamic and subtle, currentapproaches, such as rule-based or ticket driven responses struggle to react at the requiredspeed, resulting in prolonged attacker dwelltime and potential disruption of critical missionoperations, if an attack is detected at all.Real-time automated responses or self-healing' mechanisms, such as fall-back tosecure/minimum configurations, runtime policy/rule change, trusted state reconstitution, orrapid tear-down and re-deploy of compromised systems, can reduce the time required tocontain threats. The aim is to reduce attacker dwell time and maintain service continuityduring otherwise high impact incidents. This activity addresses that gap by developing anddemonstrating a proof-of-concept autonomous self-healing architecture tailored to thecritical mission operations ground segment. It will provide an adaptive resilience mechanismaddressing detection, isolation and recovery with an emphasis on service continuity. Moderntechnologies and techniques are to be explored including:- declarative infrastructure as code for cloud-agnostic redundancy and recovery automation- decoupled micro-service isolation and zero-trust architectures- secure root of trust and immutable system configuration restoration- failure prediction- adaptive response mechanisms leveraging machine learning.The proof-of-concept demonstrator will be integrated into a multi-mission, cloud nativeground segment scenario, leveraging existing (Cyber) Security Operations Centres((C)SOC) monitoring and diagnostic capabilities to ensure operational relevance. It willdemonstrate end to enddetection, isolation, and recovery in the context of missionmonitoring and control systems operating in the loop.

original.description: Objective:To design and realize a first European portable self-calibrated SI-traceable Rydberg atom-based Electric field probe.Description:Accurate measurement of electric fields is crucial for the development and operation of RF communicationsystems, particularly in space missions. Conventional antennas need fine calibration for high-integrity reception. The calibration is performed by placing uncalibrated antennas in a known EM (electromagnetic) environment that is measured via a well-calibrated antenna which creates a dependency. Whereas Rydberg based receivers allow precise measurements of RF signals which is directly related to Planck's constant and hence can self-calibrate by relying on SI (international system of units)-traceable atomic standards The activity aims to develop a portable, self-calibrated Rydberg atom based electric field probe.The probe is based on the interaction of RF-fields with Rydberg atoms, where alkali atoms are excited opticallyto Rydberg states and the applied RF-field alters the resonant state of the atoms. For this probe, the Rydbergatoms are placed in a glass vapor cell. The vapor cell acts like an RF-to-optical transducer, converting an RF Efield to an optical frequency response. The probe utilizes the concept of Electromagnetic Induced Transition (EIT), where the RF transition in the four-level atomic system causes a split of the transition spectrum for the pump laser. This splitting is measured and is directly proportional to the applied RF field amplitude. Therefore, by measuring this splitting, we get a direct measurement of the RF E-field strength. This technique could allow traceable measurements over a large frequency band including 1-500GHz. The new approach has the following benefits: 1) it will allow direct SI units linked RF E-field measurements, 2) It is self-calibrating due to atomic resonances, 3) it will provide RF field measurements independent of current techniques, 4) the probe will not perturb the field during the measurement, since no metal is present in the probe.This activity encompasses the following tasks:-Assessment of different Rydberg atom-based methods of detection of RF fields.- Requirement consolidation and performance assessment.- Detailed concept design with analysis of critical functions.- Development of the breadboard and verification in relevant environment.- Development of a technology roadmap for an EQM.

original.description: The subject of this procurement proposal is the procurement of "Operations Engineering Services in support in ESEC/Redu" covering operational services for the preparation and execution of the mission operations entrusted to the Directorate of Operations located in ESEC, including the relevant Galileo Hosting Agreements.  ESA/ESEC is the ESA European Space Security and Education Centre located in Belgium and is one of the ESA sites in Europe. The main core business in Mission Operations relevant to this procurement are:  Control dedicated Satellites and Ground Segment (so called "Small Satellite missions")  Perform its In-Orbit activities.  Host and operate some ground segment elements in support to the EU Space Programme within a secured environment - mainly Galileo and EGNOS The Operational services, within the scope specified above, will be therefore divided in two main WPs: WP-1 Small Satellites Operations:   A number of Small Satellites (such as the PROBA ones) are or will be controlled from ESEC with the help of a dedicated ground segment. In the current set-up and number of missions, up to six passes per satellite daily are supported in automatic mode for TM reception and commanding, which may be extended in the future when new missions will be operated from ESEC. The mission products are made available at ESEC and ready for distribution. The Small Satellites Mission Operations Centre is therefore responsible of the monitoring and control of the satellite and the corresponding ground segment, the handling of the user requests, the extraction of the mission products and their availability for distribution.  The Small Satellites operations concept relies on a highly automatic functioning of the ground segment and a high degree of autonomy in the space segment for the delayed execution of operations requested by telecommand and for satellite survival. No operator attended shift work is foreseen. Operational engineers supervise the small satellites mission operations and related performances usually only during normal working hours. Provisions for an On-Call service shall be also considered for the WP. Occasional working outside normal working hours and overtime may be required. The satellites are safe by design and can survive for a long period without ground station contact.   This WP will cover OPSPREP and OPS activities, support to Industry, execution of delegated tasks for critical operations (LEOP, others) together and in collaboration with Industry for this small satellite missions. This WP may implement further mission operations engineering activities carried out in support of other ESA programmes requested by ESA programme directorates to OPS. WP-2 Galileo Hosting activities:  The Galileo Hosting support will be provided in response to the requirements and agreements reached with EUSPA for Galileo and EGNOS. The provision of support to the hosting and testing activities will be performed on-site during normal working hours. Provisions for an On-Call service shall be also considered for the WP. Occasional working outside normal working hours and overtime may be required. The Agency will issue one single Invitation to Tender in Open Competition for the two WPs. Considering the relatively small volume covered by this procurement, the Tenderers will be invited to provide a single proposal covering the support to both areas.   The new contract is planned to be kicked-off starting in 1st Quarter 2027 (phase-in) as required to permit sufficient time for a smooth transition (e.g. training, certification of new service provider's personnel).  The operational phase of the contract is expected to start latest by 2nd Quarter 2027, at the expiry of the current INDUSTRIAL SERVICE PROVISION IN SUPPORT OF THE OPERATION OF ESA IN BELGIUM contract extension.
